body:
**DocPilot 3.0 — roadmap and progress.** This is not a release: no 3.0 package is published yet, and the 2.x line stays the current version on npm. This note is updated at the end of every phase. **After 3.0:** DocPilot moves to a new website and gets a new product name that does not collide with other products, so people who look for it can find it more easily. The npm package becomes `@cloflin/ai` (Phase 10); the new name and the new site are announced with the 3.0 release. **Progress:** 2 of 12 phases complete · updated 2026-10-30 ## Latest update — Phase 2: HTML extraction (2026-10-30) - `docpilot index --html-dir` and `docpilot import` share one HTML extractor. A page that fails is skipped with a warning and never stops the build, and the extractor version is part of the corpus hash of HTML corpora only. - The parser (`linkedom`) ships as a regular dependency, so `docpilot import` works after `npm i @cloflin/docpilot` with nothing else installed. A test keeps the parser out of the browser bundle. - `docPilot.html` sets `content` and `exclude` selectors per source. Without selectors, named rule lists remove navigation, footers, cookie banners, breadcrumbs, feedback widgets, share bars, bylines and in-page TOCs, and tab panels and accordions stay with their labels. - Code blocks keep their `
` lines and their language, without highlighter spans, line-number gutters or copy buttons. Links resolve against ``, then the canonical URL, then the given base, or become text with a warning. - Tables keep `colspan` / `rowspan` or fall back to a lossless row list. Heading ids, `details`, definition lists, nested lists and blockquotes survive, entities are decoded, and script, style, template and svg noise is gone. - Title, canonical URL, `lang` and `dateModified` are read before removal, and a `robots noindex` page is skipped. `docpilot import` and `docpilot doctor` print a per-source report of characters kept and dropped, empty pages, link failures and imports from an older extractor. A `fetcher` hook accepts pre-rendered HTML within the source allowlist and a timeout. - Six fixtures freeze the output byte for byte. The parse5 and Readability / defuddle spikes ran offline on 78 pages: neither beat the rule list, so nothing was adopted (engine-spec 043). - The docs, both committed indexes, both calibrations and the four frozen baselines were updated once, at the end of the phase. --- # Roadmap: DocPilot ## Overview DocPilot 3.0 widens where grounded answers come from and how fresh they stay, and shrinks what a site ships. The roadmap starts by freezing the 2.1.1 baselines and moving the existing sources onto one shared document pipeline with unchanged output bytes. Then it improves HTML extraction, builds the connectors (Intercom, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Generic REST, own-origin pages), puts the server index behind a storage adapter with an atomic hot swap, and adds the sync engine that makes an edit at the source reach answers without a restart (Core Value). Confluence and Notion follow once sync and reconcile exist. Next, one turn pipeline serves browser, server and eval, and server retrieval gains filters, a candidate pool, a reranker and contextual chunks, each backed by eval evidence. The client track then moves chat state onto a Vue-free core, splits the bundle into registered features with a custom-bundle CLI, and decides through a go/no-go whether the whole UI moves to Web Components. The last phase ships the migration path and proves the motivating case on stock DocPilot: a production site that today needs a patched DocPilot and hand-written import scripts. Two phases were added after the roadmap was created. Phase 10 puts MCP on both ends of the server runtime — an endpoint through which coding agents search the docs, and a client through which the assistant calls other services' tools — under one permission policy that only the server owner writes. Phase 11 renames the package to `@cloflin/ai` and splits it into one subpath per layer, before the release phase (Phase 12). ## Structure Notes - **Ten phases, above the standard 5-8.** 106 requirements in 11 categories split into two tracks (server: Phases 2-6, client: Phases 7-9). Research suggested 12 phases. Two merges were made where dependencies stay honest: wiki connectors joined the sync phase (they are the first schedule-first consumers of reconcile), and the turn-driver unification joined server retrieval (the driver is that phase's first deliverable and must be green before any retrieval stage lands). Further merges would cross real boundaries: Phase 1 keeps output byte-identical while Phase 2 deliberately shifts corpus hashes; Phases 4 and 5 would hold 25 requirements; Phases 7 and 8 differ in risk and research needs; Phase 9 is conditional. - **Requirements placed ahead of their category.** REL-01 (Node >= 22.13, CI on 22 and 24) is in Phase 4 because the `node:sqlite` adapter cannot run in CI before it. SYNC-08 (atomic hot swap) is in Phase 4 because the index holder is built with the store. STORE-08 (ceilings per runtime) is in Phase 1 because the shared pipeline owns the ceilings. SEC-01 to SEC-03 start in Phase 3 because credentials first exist there; later phases keep the secret scan green and extend the visibility fixtures to the wiki connectors. - **Embedding-moving changes are batched.** All extractor changes land as one extractor-version bump in Phase 2. Eval evidence for that bump, the breadcrumb prefix, the contextual prefix and the reranker is collected together in Phase 6 (EVAL-04), once the Intercom golden set exists, and always before 3.0 ships. - **The 2.x deprecation release (REL-02) is cut before 3.0 final.** The list of removed exports and options is final only after Phase 9, so Phase 12 owns it. - **Research flags.** Phases 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11 need a research pass before planning. - **Two phases were added on 2026-10-30, after the roadmap was created, and the last three were renumbered the same day.** 27 requirements in 4 new categories (MCPS, MCPC, PERM, PKG) bring the total to 133 in 15; MCPS-07 and MCPS-08 (the local and the Vercel deploy of `/mcp`) were added the same day. Phase 10 (MCP, engine-spec 042) needs the Phase 6 turn driver, where the reader's approval pause is built once for all three drivers. Phase 11 (the package split) needs the final UI (Phase 9) and the `mcp` layer (Phase 10). The release moved from Phase 10 to Phase 12. Before the renumbering, MCP was Phase 11, the package split Phase 12 and the release Phase 10; the phases run in number order, so the number order must be the dependency order. ## Phases **Phase Numbering:** - Integer phases (1, 2, 3): Planned milestone work - Decimal phases (2.1, 2.2): Urgent insertions (marked with INSERTED) Decimal phases appear between their surrounding integers in numeric order. - [x] **Phase 1: Baselines and shared document pipeline** - Freeze 2.1.1 baselines and run existing sources through one `SourceDoc` pipeline, byte-identical (completed 2026-10-30) - [x] **Phase 2: HTML extraction** - Deterministic, structure-preserving HTML to Markdown that never fails the index on one bad page (completed 2026-10-30) - [ ] **Phase 3: Source connectors and snapshot pull** - Intercom, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Generic REST and sitemap sources pulled into a snapshot that `index` reads offline - [ ] **Phase 4: Server storage and hot swap** - Server index behind a `StorageAdapter` (files, memory, SQLite, Postgres) with an atomic swap in the running server - [ ] **Phase 5: Sync engine, freshness and wiki connectors** - Edits at the source reach answers via CLI, schedule or webhook; Confluence and Notion join schedule-first - [ ] **Phase 6: Unified turn pipeline and server retrieval** - One turn driver for browser, server and eval; filters, breadcrumbs, reranker, contextual prefix, eval-gated - [ ] **Phase 7: Vue-free chat core** - Per-instance chat state on a framework-agnostic core; the Vue panel runs on it unchanged to the reader - [ ] **Phase 8: Feature registry and modular bundle** - Per-feature exports, lazy chunks, launcher, custom-bundle CLI and a published size table - [ ] **Phase 9: Web Component UI** - Evidence-based decision on a Lit `` replacing the Vue UI - [ ] **Phase 10: MCP server, MCP client and permissions** - A `/mcp` endpoint for coding agents, external MCP tools for the assistant, one owner policy that tokens and readers can only narrow - [ ] **Phase 11: Package split and rename to @cloflin/ai** - One package `@cloflin/ai` with `core`, `server`, `mcp`, `chat-ui` and `cli` subpaths, shipped before the release phase - [ ] **Phase 12: Release and acceptance** - Deprecation release, migration tooling, rc on `next`, the reference site on stock 3.0, eval no worse than 2.1.1 ## Phase Details ### Phase 1: Baselines and shared document pipeline **Goal**: The 2.1.1 behaviour is frozen as measurable baselines, and Markdown, HTML-directory and OpenAPI sources run through one shared `SourceDoc` pipeline with unchanged output bytes. **Depends on**: Nothing (first phase) **Requirements**: EVAL-01, EVAL-02, BNDL-01, CORE-02, SRC-01, SRC-02, STORE-08 **Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE): 1. The maintainer can re-run the golden eval on `rag` and `rag-local`, plus `eval --runtime=server`, and compare `rankedIds` against frozen 2.1.1 baselines kept in the repo, so a changed ranking shows up as a diff. The lexical recalibration owed since the stemmer change is done first, on the offline `rag-local` + Ollama path. 2. A bundle composition report breaks the 1.19 MB `dist/docpilot.web.js` down by contributor (Vue, Shiki, markdown-it, MiniSearch, panel code, optional features), so later phases choose what leaves from measurement. 3. Characterisation tests of the 2.1.1 session (submit sequence, state writes, citations, openers, history, quote, budget) pass on today's code and stay as the safety net for Phases 6 and 7. 4. Markdown, HTML-directory and OpenAPI sources emit documents in the one `SourceDoc` shape (id, canonical URL, title, body, `updatedAt`, locale, visibility, breadcrumb, tags, content hash), and `docs/public/rag/` and `docs/public/rag-local/` rebuild byte-identical. 5. A server-runtime corpus above the 64 KB manifest and 5 MB file ceilings builds without patching, while the browser build still refuses it. **Plans:** 12/12 plans complete in 6 waves Plans: **Wave 1** - [x] 01-01 — Characterisation harness (browser + server SSE) and the core turn: submit traces, citations, quote, history (CORE-02) - [x] 01-02 — `rankRecords` extraction, the baseline engine, `--baseline` wiring, golden repoint checkpoint (EVAL-01) - [x] 01-03 — Bundle composition report and the frozen 2.1.1 composition (BNDL-01) - [x] 01-04 — Four-source builder characterisation (the byte oracle) and the OpenAPI `dereference` test seam (SRC-02) - [x] 01-12 — SourceDoc contract and per-runtime limits, `shell.ts`, engine-spec 041 (wave 1, split from 01-04) (SRC-01, STORE-08) **Wave 2** *(blocked on Wave 1 completion)* - [x] 01-05 — Characterisation: openers, gate refusal, credential/social short-circuits, budget (CORE-02) - [x] 01-06 — Characterisation: follow-up, restore, scope change, cancel, provider error, 429 rotation (CORE-02) - [x] 01-07 — The one docs edit: register the baseline flags, browser-scoped ceiling wording, rebuild both indexes (Ollama + metered checkpoints) (EVAL-01, STORE-08) **Wave 3** *(blocked on Wave 2 completion)* - [x] 01-08 — Recalibrate rag-local (full) and rag (transfer), freeze both rankings, offline gate in verify (EVAL-02, EVAL-01) **Wave 4** *(blocked on Wave 3 completion)* - [x] 01-09 — Answer-quality and server-runtime baselines on local Ollama (EVAL-01) **Wave 5** *(blocked on Wave 4 completion)* - [x] 01-10 — All four sources through SourceDoc and `documentsToChunks`, real-corpus oracle (SRC-01, SRC-02) **Wave 6** *(blocked on Wave 5 completion)* - [x] 01-11 — Per-runtime ceilings, shell-size line, byte-identical rebuild of both indexes, phase gate (STORE-08, SRC-02) **Cross-cutting constraints:** - Every scenario goes through createHarness; this file never imports session.js (D-14) ### Phase 2: HTML extraction **Goal**: HTML pages become clean, deterministic Markdown that keeps code, links, tables and structure, and one bad page never fails `docpilot index`. **Depends on**: Phase 1 **Requirements**: HTML-01, HTML-02, HTML-03, HTML-04, HTML-05, HTML-06, HTML-07, HTML-08, HTML-09, HTML-10, HTML-11, HTML-12, HTML-13 **Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE): 1. Site owner can set `content` and `exclude` selectors per source and get only the article body. Without selectors, the rule list removes navigation, footers, cookie banners, breadcrumbs, feedback widgets, share bars and TOC sidebars, and keeps tab panels and accordions with their labels. 2. A page with `
` inside a code block produces a multi-line fenced block with the language as fence info, with highlighter spans, line-number tables and copy buttons gone. A page with an OpenAPI description embedded in an article indexes, and its relative link resolves against the canonical URL or degrades to text with a warning. 3. Heading hierarchy and ids, nested lists, GFM tables (colspan / rowspan fallback), `details`, definition lists and blockquotes survive extraction. Entities are decoded, whitespace and Unicode are normalised, and script, style, template and svg noise is gone. 4. Page title, canonical URL, `lang` and `dateModified` are extracted, a `robots noindex` page is skipped, and `docpilot import` and `docpilot doctor` print a per-source report of characters kept and dropped, empty pages and link failures. 5. After `npm i @cloflin/docpilot` on a clean machine, `docpilot import` works with nothing else installed, and the parser is absent from the browser bundle. The same HTML gives byte-identical Markdown, and the extractor version is part of the corpus hash. A Readability-class fallback is adopted only if it beats the rule list on a labelled page set, and a `fetcher` hook accepts pre-rendered HTML. **Plans:** 12/12 plans complete in 5 waves Plans: **Wave 1** - [x] 02-01 — Tracer: one `extractHtml` pipeline through `index --html-dir`, `extractor:2` in the corpus hash, per-page isolation, the link-resolver seam (HTML-07, HTML-09, HTML-03) - [x] 02-02 — `linkedom` as an exact regular dependency through `dom.ts`, parser-free bundle test, `PARSER_PINS` test (HTML-08, HTML-07) **Wave 2** *(blocked on Wave 1 completion)* - [x] 02-03 — `docPilot.html` content/exclude selectors per source, flag precedence, config validation, metadata on the document (HTML-01) - [x] 02-04 — Page metadata before removal (canonical, lang, dateModified), robots noindex, link base order and link-failure counting (HTML-06, HTML-03) - [x] 02-05 — Code blocks: `
` lines, fence language, gutters and copy chrome; OpenAPI-in-article fixture (HTML-02, HTML-13) **Wave 3** *(blocked on Wave 2 completion)* - [x] 02-06 — `docpilot import` on the shared extractor, `extractor:` stamp, extraction report, `fetcher` hook with allowlist check and timeout (HTML-10, HTML-12, HTML-06, HTML-03) - [x] 02-07 — Tables with colspan/rowspan fallback, heading ids, `details`, lists, entities, no raw HTML (HTML-04, HTML-09) - [x] 02-08 — Tab panels and accordions kept with labels; named noise lists, bylines, TOCs, figure rule; five fixtures (HTML-05, HTML-13) - [x] 02-09 — Imported pages in `index`: dead links degrade to text, stale-extractor warning (HTML-03, HTML-07) **Wave 4** *(blocked on Wave 3 completion)* - [x] 02-10 — `docpilot doctor` extraction report and stale imports (HTML-10) - [x] 02-11 — Fixture snapshots, parse5 and Readability/defuddle spikes offline, engine-spec 043, adopt only on evidence (HTML-11, HTML-13, HTML-07) **Wave 5** *(blocked on Wave 4 completion; metered step behind the owner's approval)* - [x] 02-12 — The one docs step (D-18): register flags and `docPilot.html`, edit docs, rebuild both indexes, recalibrate, q-46 fix, re-take the four baselines (HTML-01, HTML-08, HTML-10, HTML-12) **Cross-cutting constraints:** - No metered, hosted or LAN-model call outside plan 02-12, and that one only after the price check and the owner's "yes" - No plan before 02-12 edits docs/**/*.md, docs/public/rag*/, docpilot/baselines/ or docpilot/golden.jsonl - Fixtures are synthetic and brand-free; the reference vendor is never named in a tracked file ### Phase 3: Source connectors and snapshot pull **Goal**: Site owner can pull public content from Intercom, Zendesk, Freshdesk, any JSON API and their own origin into a snapshot directory that `docpilot index` turns into an index, with no hand-written import script and no credential leaving the build machine. **Depends on**: Phase 2 (HTML-bodied connectors reuse the extractor), Phase 1 **Requirements**: SRC-03, SRC-04, SRC-05, SRC-06, SRC-07, SRC-08, SRC-09, SRC-10, SRC-11, SRC-12, SRC-13, CONN-01, CONN-02, CONN-03, CONN-06, CONN-07, CONN-08, SEC-01, SEC-02, SEC-03 **Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE): 1. Site owner can run `docpilot pull` for an Intercom Help Center (published articles only, per-locale state, collection breadcrumbs, pinned `Intercom-Version`), a Zendesk Help Center (incremental endpoint, translations) and a Freshdesk knowledge base (category and folder walk) and get a snapshot directory of Markdown plus front-matter. Each (article, locale) pair is one document. `docpilot index` then reads only files and makes no network call. 2. When an API call fails, `docpilot pull` keeps the last good snapshot of that source and reports the failure. Pulls retry on 429 and 5xx honouring `Retry-After`, resume pagination, and lose no document to an `updated_at` tie or clock skew. `docpilot connectors test ` reports auth result, first page, field coverage and locale / state counts and writes nothing. 3. Site owner can write their own connector against the exported `Connector` interface, or configure Generic REST declaratively (auth, pagination, array path, field map, incremental parameter, delete detection, `transform`). Generic REST refuses private, loopback and link-local targets unless allowlisted. Site owner can map citation URLs with `urlTemplate`, include or exclude collections and labels before import, and see source tags in chunk metadata. 4. Site owner can point a sitemap / URL source at their own origin and get its pages with no import script: sitemap discovery, robots, 1 request/s by default, a cookie jar for geo-redirects, a configurable user agent. A WAF soft-block or stub page is reported and not indexed. 5. Draft, internal and restricted documents never reach an index (per-connector fixtures prove it), and the static build refuses any non-public document. Connector, store and sync config and credentials never appear in the client config, built bundle, manifest or logs; credentials come only from environment-variable references; `npm run verify` scans the built output for them; `docpilot doctor` checks connector auth and scopes. **Plans:** 16 plans in 7 waves Plans: **Wave 1** - [ ] 03-01 — Tracer: a site owner's own `Connector` → `runPull` → the one normaliser → the snapshot → the existing kb reader → `index`, with no network (SRC-03, SRC-11) - [ ] 03-16 — The index side of the snapshot: the kb reader reads `tags`, `breadcrumb` and `visibility`, `pages[].tags`, `tagScope`, the no-network preload (SRC-10, SRC-11) **Wave 2** *(blocked on Wave 1 completion)* - [ ] 03-02 — The one fetch kit: retry and `Retry-After`, rate-limit pause, budget, concurrency, five pagination modes; the SSRF guard with the IANA block list; the redactor; `fetchWithin` awaits its check (SRC-04, CONN-07, SEC-02) - [ ] 03-03 — Byte-order walk in both walks, the kb dot-skip, `index` stops on an interrupted swap and warns while a pull runs (SRC-11, SRC-12) - [ ] 03-04 — Last good snapshot: per-source lock, crash recovery, the three delete paths, held pages, the zero-document and blocked-share guards, cursor written last, `--full`, `--dry` (SRC-03, SRC-05, SRC-11, SRC-12) - [ ] 03-05 — The normaliser complete: html, markdown and text bodies, links, citations (`urlTemplate`, `url(doc)`, allowlist at pull time), include and exclude, locales, the visibility gate, signed-URL degrade (SRC-06, SRC-07, SRC-08, SRC-09, SRC-10, SEC-01) **Wave 3** *(blocked on Wave 2 completion)* - [ ] 03-06 — `docPilot.connectors` validated before any request, `*Env` credentials and one run-wide redactor, the built-in types by name, Generic REST with every pagination mode (SRC-03, SRC-04, CONN-06, CONN-07, SEC-02) **Wave 4** *(blocked on Wave 3 completion)* - [ ] 03-07 — Generic REST complete: every auth mode, the shared OAuth client-credentials token source, incremental, deletes, `transform`, `itemUrl` (CONN-06, SRC-05, SEC-02) - [ ] 03-08 — Intercom Help Center: version 2.17, per-locale state, staged changes held, audience default-deny, collection breadcrumbs (CONN-01, SRC-06, SRC-08, SEC-03) - [ ] 03-09 — Freshdesk: category → folder → article walk, status and visibility codes as flagged constants, default language only, 1 request/s (CONN-03, SRC-06, SEC-03) - [ ] 03-10 — Sitemap / URL source: discovery through robots.txt, nested indexes and gzip, RFC 9309 rules, 1 request/s, cookie jar, WAF markers, the owner's fetcher (CONN-08, SEC-03) - [ ] 03-11 — `docpilot connectors test` and the doctor connectors block with `--connectors` (SRC-13, SEC-02) **Wave 5** *(blocked on Wave 4 completion)* - [ ] 03-12 — Zendesk: OAuth with `hc:read`, the incremental feed, one document per translation, restrictions, the translation sweep, the warned per-locale fallback (CONN-02, SRC-05, SRC-06, SRC-08, SEC-03) - [ ] 03-13 — SEC-01 canary and shape scan and the browser-graph check inside verify; the public `./connectors` subpath and `types/connectors.d.ts` (SEC-01, SEC-02, SRC-03) **Wave 6** *(blocked on Wave 5 completion)* - [ ] 03-14 — Engine-spec 044, "Connectors and the snapshot pull", and its README row (SRC-03, SRC-11, CONN-07) **Wave 7** *(blocked on Wave 6 completion)* - [ ] 03-15 — The one docs step (D-31): registration, docs, both indexes rebuilt, both calibrations, the four baselines re-taken; the metered step waits for the owner's approval (SRC-03, SRC-11, SRC-13, SEC-01, SEC-02) **Cross-cutting constraints:** - No metered, hosted or LAN-model call outside plan 03-15, and that one only after the price check and the owner's "yes"; no plan calls a vendor API with a credential (the live vendor checks are the owner's manual verification, D-28) - No plan before 03-15 edits docs/**/*.md, docs/public/rag*/, docpilot/baselines/, docpilot/golden.jsonl, or the registration in src/config.ts, src/cli-flags.ts and bin/docpilot.js (D-10, D-31) - Fixtures are synthetic and brand-free; the reference vendor is never named in a tracked file; connector code runs on Node 20 and adds no runtime dependency (D-29) **Research**: Per-connector spikes on live trial accounts: Zendesk deletions in the incremental export, Freshdesk article `updated_at`, Intercom webhook topics for the account's API version, signature details. Zendesk auth is OAuth client credentials with `hc:read`, not an API token (https://developer.zendesk.com/documentation/authentication/oauth-migration/); confirm which Help Center endpoints, the incremental export included, accept that scope. ### Phase 4: Server storage and hot swap **Goal**: The server index lives behind a `StorageAdapter` that works on files, memory, SQLite and Postgres, and a running server swaps to updated content atomically without a restart. **Depends on**: Phase 1 (independent of Phases 2 and 3; can run in parallel with them) **Requirements**: STORE-01, STORE-02, STORE-03, STORE-04, STORE-05, STORE-06, STORE-07, STORE-09, STORE-10, SYNC-08, REL-01 **Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE): 1. An existing `rag/` directory loads unchanged through the files adapter and answers as it did in 2.1.1 (the Phase 1 baselines show no regression). 2. Site owner can keep the server index in SQLite through `node:sqlite` with no extra install, or in Postgres with pgvector by passing their own `pg` client (the package imports no database driver). One exported adapter conformance suite passes against the files, memory, SQLite and Postgres adapters. 3. Replacing one document is atomic, so a reader never sees a half-updated article, and the sync cursor commits together with the documents. The store records embedding model, dimensions and quantisation, and the server refuses to start or sync on a mismatch. 4. When a document changes in the store from outside the server process, the running server serves the new content without a restart, and an in-flight turn finishes on the index it started with. 5. `docpilot store migrate ` moves an index between adapters without re-embedding. A lease keeps a second instance from holding the same source lock. `engines.node` is `>= 22.13` and CI runs Node 22 and 24. **Plans:** 14 plans in 8 waves Plans: **Wave 1** - [ ] 04-01 — Tracer: one identity module (hash, df, manifest, names) and the static writer shared by `docpilot index` and the store; committed rag-local round-trips through store records byte for byte; int8 for server builds (STORE-01, STORE-03) - [ ] 04-02 — Node floor 22.13: engines, lockfile root, CI `['22.13.0', '24']`, Node-20 comments outside docs/; spike S2 (`node:sqlite` on exactly 22.13.0) (REL-01, STORE-04) - [ ] 04-03 — Spikes S1 (MiniSearch build and stall at 10k/50k) and S3 (PGlite, pglite-socket, pg in a scratch dir after the D-42 checks) (SYNC-08, STORE-05, STORE-06) **Wave 2** *(blocked on Wave 1 completion)* - [ ] 04-04 — StorageAdapter contract, foldCommit, memory adapter, memory leases, the exported framework-free conformance suite, types/store.d.ts (STORE-01, STORE-02, STORE-06, STORE-07, STORE-09) **Wave 3** *(blocked on Wave 2 completion)* - [ ] 04-05 — Files adapter: rag/ loads unchanged and replays 2.1.1, integrity-checked reads, file leases and the writer lock, the two-phase sidecar, the suite on files (STORE-03, STORE-02, STORE-06, STORE-09) - [ ] 04-06 — Index holder: pin per turn, single-flight swap, refusals before assembly, the two-generation bound, polling; WeakMap lexical cache with async prepare (SYNC-08, STORE-07) **Wave 4** *(blocked on Wave 3 completion)* - [ ] 04-07 — SQLite adapter on `node:sqlite`: lazy import, WAL, busy pragma, Uint8Array BLOBs, paged snapshots, leases, defensive, the suite on SQLite (STORE-04, STORE-06) **Wave 5** *(blocked on Wave 4 completion)* - [ ] 04-08 — The server over the holder: any store as `index`, `server.store`, start-up refusals, per-generation shell and ETag, store facts in /metrics, close/refresh, the D-23 concurrency proof (SYNC-08, STORE-07, STORE-03) - [ ] 04-09 — Postgres adapter over the owner's `pg` client: pinned test devDependencies after D-42 checks, `vec bytea` plus pgvector column, REPEATABLE READ snapshots, the suite on PGlite, gated real run (STORE-05, STORE-06) **Wave 6** *(blocked on Wave 5 completion)* - [ ] 04-10 — `docpilot serve`, the VitePress dev server and eval on the store, each closing what it opens (SYNC-08, STORE-03, STORE-04) - [ ] 04-11 — `store migrate` (migrateStore, runStore) with refusals, replace, dry run and lease; the committed rag-local through every adapter keeps its hash and frozen ranking (STORE-10, STORE-06) - [ ] 04-12 — The `./store` public subpath, the layering rule in check-docpilot.sh, the bundle assertion (STORE-01, STORE-06) **Wave 7** *(blocked on Wave 6 completion)* - [ ] 04-13 — Spike S4 (snapshot read per adapter) and S1 on the shipped build; engine-spec 045 and its README row (all phase IDs, design record) **Wave 8** *(blocked on Wave 7 completion; metered step behind the owner's approval)* - [ ] 04-14 — The one docs step (D-28): register `store migrate`, document the store, hot swap and Node 22.13, rebuild both indexes, recalibrate, re-take the four baselines (STORE-10, REL-01) **Cross-cutting constraints:** - No metered, hosted or LAN-model call outside plan 04-14, and that one only after the price check and the owner's "yes" - No plan before 04-14 edits docs/**/*.md, docs/public/rag*/, docpilot/baselines/ or docpilot/golden.jsonl; test the SQLite vector path with `defensive` on. ### Phase 5: Sync engine, freshness and wiki connectors **Goal**: An edit at the source reaches the running server's answers without a rebuild or restart, by CLI, schedule or webhook, with reconcile as the correctness backstop;
